liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (2 reviews): Jerry plays with great energy from the very start of Half-Step; Prolonged instrumental ending of Half-Step into Franklin's Tower and Stranger made a really nice opening [16][20]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review, 1 other source): Second-set opening through Eyes has a different swing; reviewer attended the show; A 37-second patch from the Nakamichi 700 source fills the jam out of Eyes Of The World [7][27]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer, not usually a Rooster fan, found this version really hot [20]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 other source): Brokedown Palace is listed as the encore [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-05-09.mtx.seamons.ht10.118878.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 183 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1981-05-09.mtx.seamons.92246.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 181 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Matrix sounds obviously better than the reviewer's old cassette of the show [27]
- **gd1981-05-09.sbd.miller.33930.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 178 min; rated 2.88/5 by 8 [3]. Said about its sound: Super sound quality, though there is a patch after Black Peter; Soundboard has some hiss between songs; Charlie Miller's transfer work on the soundboard is praised as excellent [20][23][26]
- **gd81-05-09.glassberg.17699.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 179 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds good, especially given Nassau's usual poor acoustics; Audience recording sounds distant and dull at low volume, but opens up when turned up [16][18]
- **gd1981-05-09.153007.nak500.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 23 songs; 181 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says many federal agents were around Nassau, with DEA in the parking lot before this tour [21]
- Reviewer recalls Garcia saying beforehand he would not subject fans to those agents again [21]
- Reviewer bought a cheap backstage pass this night; stick-on passes got you everywhere then [21]
- Among 1981 setlists and performances, reviewer thinks this show is hard to top [16]
- Reviewer suggests pairing this show with the 5/6 release would have shown the band in 1981, before Bobby's "HAAH!" years [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-05-09.mtx.seamons.ht10.118878.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix of SBD (shnid=33930) and AUDs (shnid=17699 & 32883) by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN > AIFF > Final Cut > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity >… [1]
- **gd1981-05-09.mtx.seamons.92246.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: MATRIX MIX: 1 SBD/2 AUD (About 60%/40%) [2]. Also: Matrix mix of one soundboard and two audience sources, about 60%/40%, transferred and mastered by Charlie Miller; Barry Glassberg taped with Nak 700s front of board; Rob Eaton used Senn 421 plus PZM mix; Patches in Eyes Of The World and from Black Peter to the end come from Eaton's mix [2]
- **gd1981-05-09.sbd.miller.33930.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat [3]. Also: Glassberg's Nak 700 supplies the first five seconds of Half Step; Eaton's Senn 421 and PZM mix supplies patches [3]
- **gd81-05-09.glassberg.17699.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's [6]
- **gd1981-05-09.153007.nak500.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi DM-500 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII) [7]. Also: Master recording came from Jim Vita; Charlie Miller transferred it; Mark Severson's Nakamichi 700 source supplies two patches [7]
